title: Trimlight, Jellyfish, Celebright, EverLights and Oelo: Dealer Brands Explained
metaTitle: Trimlight, Jellyfish, Celebright, EverLights and Oelo
metaDescription: What Trimlight, Jellyfish, Celebright, EverLights and Oelo publish on voltage, warranty and price, what none publish in CA$, and which have a DIY option.
excerpt: Five installed permanent lighting brands, set side by side using only what each publishes. We cover voltage, light type, warranty, posted prices and currency, cold ratings, and which ones will sell you a kit to install yourself.
heroAlt: Home with permanent lighting track installed along the roofline in daylight
keyTakeaways: All five brands sell lights in a channel under the eave and quote by the job. None publishes an installed price in CA$.
Trimlight, Jellyfish and Oelo post price figures with no currency stated. EverLights posts one DIY kit price. Celebright posts none.
Published voltages differ: Trimlight 12V, Celebright and EverLights 24V, Oelo 36V, Jellyfish 48V.
Warranties run from 5 years on parts (Jellyfish) to 10 years (Celebright) to a lifetime product warranty (Trimlight). Ours is 5 years on parts.
Oelo and EverLights sell DIY kits online, Jellyfish sells one by quote, and Trimlight says a DIY kit cancels its lifetime warranty.

body.text: Short answer: these five brands all sell lights in a channel under the eave, and all five quote by the job through a dealer or their own crew. Trimlight, Jellyfish and Oelo post price figures with no currency stated. EverLights posts one DIY kit price. Celebright, the Canadian one, posts none. None of the five publishes an installed price in Canadian dollars. Four have a DIY route of some kind: Oelo and EverLights sell kits online, Jellyfish sells one by quote, and Trimlight says some dealers sell kits but that buying one cancels its lifetime warranty.

body.text: Trimlight

Trimlight is based in Utah and says it is sold and installed by authorized dealers across the United States and Canada. Its 3L light is listed at 12V, RGB, three LEDs, 0.9 W, IP68, 50,000 plus hours, with 6, 9 or 12 inch spacing and 30 to 60 lumens depending on how it is measured. The aluminum channel comes in more than 50 standard colours. Control is the Trimlight Edge app on 2.4 GHz WiFi, with Google Home and Alexa. The warranty is a lifetime product warranty, with dealer labour covered for at least one year. The 3L page also notes: "Daytime usage may void the warranty." No cold rating is published.
Trimlight is a good fit if you want a dealer install with a wide choice of channel colours and a lifetime product warranty, and you have a dealer nearby.
Jellyfish Lighting

Jellyfish is a US company. Its eave lights run at 48V with a 12V controller, in full-spectrum RGB with white adjustable from 2200K to 7000K. Spacing is 6, 9 or 16 inches and the rating is IP67. It is one of the few brands that publishes a temperature range: -40 °C to +55 °C. Warranty on the eave lights is 5 years on parts and 1 year on labour. The controller works on 2.4 GHz WiFi and, the page says, also without WiFi. Lumens and rated hours are not published. Its locations page describes more than 400 US locations and lists none in Canada.
Jellyfish is a good fit if a published -40 °C rating matters to you and you can get it installed or shipped where you live. Ask about Canada before you plan around it.
Celebright

Celebright is headquartered in Ottawa and installs through dealers across North America. It publishes a 24V system with RGBW lights, a 90 plus CRI, and construction to UL 2108 and CSA C22.2 standards. The free Celebright Cloud app runs on Android and iPhone, with Google Home, Alexa and IFTTT. The warranty is 10 years on all system components and transfers to a new owner, for systems bought on or after 1 January 2025. Spacing, lumens, an IP rating and a cold rating in degrees are not published, and neither is a price.
Celebright is a good fit if you want a Canadian company, a dealer install and a 10-year transferable warranty, and you are comfortable getting a quote.
EverLights

EverLights, a US company, offers professional installation and a DIY line called ClickLights. The kit is 24V with RGBW lights, listed at 70 lumens, IP68 and 50,000 hours, in an aluminum channel with screw-on caps. Control is the EverLights app through a wired bridge, with Google Home and Alexa. On warranty, its pages differ: the home page says 1 year labour and 5 years parts, the DIY page says one year on the equipment, and the bundle page says 3 years on parts. Ask which applies to what you are buying. Shipping to Canada is not published.
EverLights is a good fit if it serves your area and you want either a pro install or a boxed kit from the same maker.
Oelo

Oelo is a US maker that states its product is made in the USA. It publishes more price detail than the other four. The system is 36V with RGB lights rated IP68, in an acrylic or metal channel in 10 colours. Its 100 ft kit lists 130 lights. Rated life is 100,000 hours. The warranty is 7 years on dealer installs and 5 years on contractor or DIY installs. DIY kits from 25 to 550 ft are sold online. Its quote form accepts Canadian addresses, but shipping kits to Canada is not stated on the pages we read. No cold rating in degrees is published.
Oelo is a good fit if you want a DIY kit from a brand that also has installers, and you like the option of an acrylic cover over the lights.

body.text: Trimlight calls its range national averages and not a quote. Jellyfish adds that most homeowners spend between $3,000 and $6,000 (currency not stated, a US company). Oelo calls its installed figures starting prices. For a Canadian house, get a written quote and ask whether it is in CA$, what the labour warranty is, and who comes back if a light fails.
Where we sit

We are not a dealer network and we do not offer a lifetime warranty. Celebright's 10 years and Trimlight's lifetime product warranty are both longer than our 5 years on parts. What we do differently is post the price. Our kits are 12V RGBW lights in aluminum track, sized from 50 to 250 ft, with free shipping anywhere in Canada. See current kit prices at /diy-kits and shipping details at /shipping-returns before you compare. You install a kit yourself with a drill and a ladder, or our own crew installs in Southwestern Ontario. Forever Lights is a sister brand run by the same parent company as Illumi, Master Decker Inc., and uses the same family of 12V track hardware.

Gemstone Lights, the Calgary dealer brand, has its own article at /resources/gemstone-lights-vs-diy-track-lighting-kits and the retail string brands are in /resources/govee-permanent-outdoor-lights-vs-track-lighting for comparison. For what the voltage column changes, see /resources/track-lights-vs-string-lights-permanent-outdoor-lighting and for every name in one table see /brands on this site.

faq.q: Which dealer-installed permanent lighting brands are Canadian?
faq.a: Of the five in this article, Celebright is headquartered in Ottawa. Trimlight, Jellyfish, EverLights and Oelo are US companies. Trimlight says it has authorized dealers in Canada. Gemstone Lights, covered in a separate article, was founded in Calgary.

faq.q: How much do Trimlight or Jellyfish lights cost per foot?
faq.a: As listed on 27 November 2026, Trimlight posts $18 to $35 per linear foot installed and Jellyfish posts $25 to $35. Neither page states a currency and both are US companies. Neither publishes a price in CA$.
No. Celebright says the main cost driver is the number of linear feet installed and offers free estimates through its dealers. We found no posted price per foot.

faq.q: Which of these brands sell a DIY kit?
faq.a: Oelo and EverLights sell DIY kits online. Jellyfish offers a DIY kit by quote. Trimlight says some dealers sell DIY kits but that choosing one cancels the lifetime product warranty. Celebright does not mention a DIY option.

faq.q: Which dealer brand has the longest warranty?
faq.a: Trimlight lists a lifetime product warranty and Celebright lists 10 years, transferable to a new owner. Oelo lists 7 years on dealer installs, and Jellyfish lists 5 years on parts and 1 on labour. Our own warranty is 5 years on parts.
